bridgeDispatchCoverage.trace: Runtime command/config caller → readBridgeInput → NativeCommandBridge.handle → native pending reply/notification → caller. Payload remains open; check envelope (B03/B23).
ProviderSession initialize → ingress → fixed bridge init/ack results → connection readiness. Unused params intentionally unknown; structural request envelope still checked (P01/B01).

Runtime catalog/diagnostics caller → ingress → SDK account/models/commands or live bridge activity → satisfies HandlerResult → provider diagnostics/catalog consumers. Typed SDK sources; native identity and unknown rate limits preserved (B04/B06/B09/M04).

Retained move caller → ingress → version/account/exact proof and session export/import → persisted movement evidence → runtime retained move outcome. Preserve exact tool JSON, hashes, native state and uncertain write receipts (B01/B17/B18/B20).

Runtime thread caller → ingress → session-store create/load/list and native history projections → typed session/thread DTO → runtime history/provider consumer. Current inputs can be decoded; historic Session compatibility must be proved (B01/B11/B13).

Retained workspace/control request → ingress → exact native turn/checkpoint proofs, control receipt → SDK rewind/fork/compaction → persisted Session and typed result. Types cannot replace exact boundary, file verification or unknown outcome (B01/B14/B16/B22).

Runtime retained input → ingress → session/account/preparation guard + provenance grouping → SDK query/input/interrupt → persisted turn/delivery and typed response. Preserve split-native-id and partial-cancel uncertainty (B01/B04/B06/B22).

Runtime settings/control/view caller → ingress → owned Session/settings/task/file/repair operations → typed HandlerResult or legacy repair data → runtime UI/control consumer. Decode request shapes, retain idle/source/task authority and persisted format proof (B01/B11/B15/B16/B22).

Runtime command/task view/control → ingress → active-query typed task/queue map or guarded SDK background result → typed result. Preserve task identity/eligibility and native receipt evidence (B01/B22).

Runtime MCP caller → ingress → active SDK connection catalog/reconnect → typed result with external config/schema tails open. Do not equate a compile-time SDK type with actual reconnection evidence (B01/B18).
Runtime skills caller → ingress → roots/session plus native settings/plugin catalog → typed skill output. Request is first-party; installed registry versions need deeper producer proof (B01/B21).

categoryRules.codeSourceExtension: /\.(?:rs|[cm]?tsx?|[cm]?jsx?|py|sh)$/; .sql fixture is counted as test/non-code and still mechanically scanned
categoryRules.metadata: All remaining tracked paths (16), including package/Cargo/tsconfig/readme/layout/asset-extension owners, mechanically scanned but not counted as handwritten production code.
categoryRules.vendor: path containing /vendor/ or /node_modules/ (none tracked within roots)

census.exactExclusions: No tracked file under assigned roots excluded from the mechanical text scan. Recommendations target handwritten production code. Every test, generated and metadata path excluded from that target is explicitly recorded by category in trackedManifest. Untracked files, dependency checkouts, build outputs and all live/runtime-state paths excluded. Adjacent owner files are read-only traces, outside census totals.
census.hashDefinition: SHA-256 of repository-relative paths sorted lexicographically, one LF after every path including the last; UTF-8. No file-content hash is implied.

classificationLegend.already typed: The inspected ingress/projection already has a named type/decoder or has no raw JSON boundary. Runtime identity/policy/evidence checks still apply.
classificationLegend.remove Value via direct typed decode/own: At a true interpreting boundary, replace ad hoc JSON tree access with owner-backed Deserialize (Rust) or checked schema-derived decode (TypeScript). At typed→JSON→typed internal paths, construct the owner type directly. A plain TS annotation/as assertion is not decoding.
classificationLegend.retain justified opaque/raw boundary: Payload belongs to an external/open protocol, exact proof/hash, generic journal patch or presentation-only path. Type consumed projections without destroying the raw representation.
classificationLegend.unresolved needs deeper proof: Potential improvement identified, but producer/legacy/migration/signature compatibility is not yet sufficiently established to recommend deleting checks.

constraintsObserved: No builds, tests, package installs, source edits, live service/credential/state reads, native provider calls, or delivery actions. Baseline Linux compile issue intentionally excluded. No implementation/failing or passing test evidence claimed.

coverageDefinitions.deep: Read cited boundary sections and their immediate producer/decode/consumer paths for the 57 family rows; grouped all 47 bridge handle cases. This is family-based source tracing, not every line manually read. Existing typed owners and compatibility guards were examined before recommending a new projection.
coverageDefinitions.mechanical: git ls-tree -r --name-only at the pinned commit (checked against git ls-files inventory), then git show for every tracked file under the seven roots. 317/317 text files scanned with the recorded lexical pattern. 278 files match the code-source extension filter; all remaining metadata/fixtures were still mechanically read. 89/107 production files have expanded lexical hits. Pattern matches include comments, type parameters, map.get, strings and inline tests; they are not defect counts.
coverageDefinitions.testsAndGenerated: All test/generated text was mechanically scanned and counted, but tests were not run or exhaustively reviewed as behavioral witnesses. 27 production Rust files contain cfg(test) sections: production file/line counts include those sections; no production-only LOC claim.
coverageDefinitions.triage: 27 remaining production files are listed separately; their hits are typed helpers/SDK adapters, plain byte/process I/O, maps, comments or inline tests, with no additional JSON decoding family identified. They were mechanically scanned and selected hit contexts inspected, not every callgraph deeply reviewed.
coverageDefinitions.unresolved: Rows marked unresolved name the exact missing producer/history/owner proof. A complete mechanical census does not establish that historical persisted values can all be decoded by a proposed stricter type.

executiveSummary: All 317 tracked files were read mechanically. 107 handwritten production code files; 180 test/fixture/test-config files; 14 generated files; 16 repository metadata/docs/config assets; 0 vendor. 57 boundary-family rows and all 47 bridge dispatch cases are classified. 24 typed-decoding/owned-construction opportunities, 13 justified raw boundaries, 10 already-typed families, 10 compatibility/proof follow-ups. These are source-level maintainability/contract observations, not reproduced runtime defects.
limits: No runtime bugs reproduced and no live success proved. All witnesses are proposals; the known Linux compile failure was neither investigated nor used to limit source analysis.
Exact historic session/monitor/account/receipt/config corpora and external native registry versions were not read from live state. Migration-dependent recommendations remain unresolved.

Lexical scanning is broad but is not an AST/exhaustiveness proof; in particular, opaque data can flow through aliases/imported APIs with no Value token in a file. Caller traces cover the listed boundary families, not all application behavior.
Tables include cross-root source references only where needed to follow an assigned-root boundary. Other agents own full censuses of those packages.
preservationRules: Preserve provider unknown methods, extension fields, unused unknown params, arbitrary tool inputSchema and external error data; known method names alone do not justify a closed global native protocol.

Preserve exact request/op identities, request-to-method correlation, generations, journal cursor/ack visibility, content digests, pending receipt state and late-reply evidence. Decode failure after possible submission remains unknown.

Peer fallback is safe only on explicit sent:false. Malformed/missing sent, body/read failure after transmission, or invalid response must remain uncertain; never turn a schema rejection into permission to resend.

Verify signed peer bodies and canonical receipts using the original complete representation. Decode a narrow projection after verification; do not drop extensions or change numeric/order semantics before proof.

Legacy session/journal/history records may legitimately omit fields fresh records require. Shape validation cannot replace complete native history, pinned path/identity, idle state, explicit metadata-loss approval or fresh credential evidence.

Reuse one named owner/generated contract; do not add parallel local schemas. Primitive shape checks may move into decoders; authorization, bounds, identities, freshness, ordering and semantic proof checks remain.
priorityMeaning: P1 = highest-value boundary-contract/duplication follow-up; P2 = useful simplification; P3 = smaller/local follow-up. Priority is not a vulnerability severity or confirmed runtime impact.
